task_message:
Case V63: segment the vascular soft-tissue tumor on this T2-weighted MRI.

Volume: 241x241x89 voxels, 1 mm isotropic. Budgets: max 40 tool calls / 15 model prompts / 10 min wall time.
Start with `seg_open`. Finish with `seg_finish`.
final_assistant_text:
Case V63 finished. Summary of the work:

**Findings**
- The T2-weighted volume (241×241×89, 1 mm) shows a markedly hyperintense, multi-lobulated soft-tissue mass in the right lateral abdominal wall/flank, extending cranio-caudally over ~6 cm, with a bright core, internal dark flow-void-like dots and a less intense periphery. Skin fiducial markers (small bright ovals at the surface) and the normal right kidney (posteromedial) were distinguished from the lesion.

**Segmentation**
1. `seg_open` + axial/coronal/sagittal sheets located the lesion (right flank, axial ~12–76, coronal ~96–142, sagittal ~170–202).
2. A positive point on the bright core (v1, 19 mL) captured the mass.
3. `seg_candidates` proposed surrounding tissue; the contiguous rim (C1) was accepted (v2) and `seg_refine` smoothed it (v3, 40 mL); clearly non-lesion proposals (fat bands, markers) were rejected.
4. Two negative points trimmed the over-extended dim superior cap (v4, 27.2 mL, single component).
5. Final review (5 slices/plane + candidates) showed the lesion well covered, with no convincing missed lesion tissue in the past-the-mask panels; remaining candidates were fat/fascia and were rejected.

Final mask: one component, 27.2 mL, saved with **medium** confidence (the extent of the less intense periphery versus adjacent fat is the main residual uncertainty).
